predecessors.name: French Indochina
predecessors.text: Vietnam less the Viet Minh base at Tuyên Quang and the Central Highlands, the state formed on 14 June 1949 from Cochinchina, Annam and Tonkin

successors.name: Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnam)
successors.text: the southern zone of the Geneva Accords: 'a temporary division of Vietnam at the 17th parallel'

ledger.x: 1949: the State of Vietnam is formed on 14 June as an associated state in the French Union under Bảo Đại, after the Élysée Accords of 8 March and the National Assembly's approval of Cochinchina's reunification on 20 May.
1949: the State of Vietnam takes the French side of the war against the Viet Minh.
1949: the State of Vietnam is an associated state of the French Union, mirroring french-indochina's vassal_start of June 1949.
1950: the Central Highlands become the Domain of the Crown on 15 April; 'the old French colonial administrators remained in power' in Kontum, Pleiku and Darlac, and Dalat was its capital.
1954: full independence from France, mirroring french-indochina's vassal_end of June 1954.
1954: Vietnam is divided at the 17th parallel.
1954: the fighting ends with the Geneva Accords of 21 July.
1955: Diệm proclaims the Republic of Vietnam on 26 October after the referendum of 23 October ('widely known as South Vietnam'); the Domain of the Crown had been dissolved in March.

wars.name: First Indochina War
wars.outcome: The Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954 divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel, the State of Vietnam taking the south.

certainty.note: The state's de facto hold over the countryside was contested by the Viet Minh; only the cities and the Domain of the Crown are firm.
The 17th parallel line of the Geneva Accords.
